## Nod reaches you on Telegram and WhatsApp 📱

Schedule results, nudges and other messages Nod starts on its own now also go to Telegram or WhatsApp. They go to the one you wrote from last. Everything still shows in the Nod app.

Linking now checks that it's really you. On Telegram, you press **Start** in your bot's chat. On WhatsApp, you write in **Message yourself** on the linked phone. To write from another phone, select **Write from another phone** and send the message that opens.

**Channels** shows when your last message arrived. When you ask Nod why a channel is quiet, it can now check that channel instead of guessing.

If Telegram or WhatsApp stopped answering you, link again in **Channels**. On Telegram, open **Manage Telegram**, select **Link another account** and press **Start**. On WhatsApp, write in **Message yourself**, or select **Write from another phone**.

## Fixed in this release

- **Remembering:** When you ask Nod to remember something, it now saves it in any language. Before, it often saved nothing.
- **Computer clock:** Telegram and WhatsApp messages no longer go missing when your computer's clock is wrong.

Mac requires macOS 14 or later. Windows requires Windows 11 with WSL 2. Linux needs Flatpak and a desktop secret store. A local Linux assistant also needs KVM. To install, follow the [install guide](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/get-started/install-desktop/). Mac, Windows and Linux apps download their runtime on first launch. Mac and Windows apps update themselves; Linux updates by installing the next bundle. Check nod-linux-x64.flatpak against SHA256SUMS-linux-x64 before installation.

Mac builds use Developer ID signing and Apple notarization. Windows builds are signed by n8n GmbH. The Linux bundle has a checksum. Public releases include build provenance.

Jobs that eat an afternoon of tabs, logins, and forms.

Say once that Anna, not Bob, handles invoices. It remembers.

Every note, visible.
See, edit, or forget each one, with the message it came from.		 Drafts that sound like you.
Learns your style from sent emails, with no names or numbers.
Tell it once.
Say something changed, and it uses the new fact from then on.		 It learns how to do a task.
Reuses the steps, and fixes them when a site changes.

It learns about you only from your own messages, never from the pages or emails it reads.
How memory works


- **Runs on your computer or server.** Files, memory, and saved logins stay there. Your model provider gets what each task needs. - **Uses the model you choose.** OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure, 20+ more, or your own server. Or sign in with ChatGPT Plus or Pro. - **Follows your rules.** The server checks each app action, and each website step that can change something, against your request and rules. Anything they don't cover waits for your yes. - **Keeps secrets out of the model.** Vault enters passwords, codes, and cards privately on the website. - **Shows what it did.** Every action and sign-in is in Usage, with costs and a monthly limit on API models.

Architecture · Agent runtime · Security model


- **Managed hosting.** An always-on Nod, hosted for you. - **Make phone calls.** For the errands that still need a voice. - **Nod for your team.** Share one Nod, with its apps and memory. - **Make it your own.** Add your own skills and tools without touching the core.

What does it cost?
Nod is free and open source. You bring your own model provider, which bills you directly. With an API model selected, Nod [shows what each task cost](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/use/spending/) and stops at your monthly limit.
Do I need n8n?
No. Nod is its own app, made by the team behind [n8n](https://n8n.io). It is not the n8n AI Assistant.
Where does my data go?
Your files, memory, and saved logins stay on the machine running Nod. Your model provider gets what each task needs, and app connections go through a connection service that n8n hosts by default. Nod also shares basic usage data with n8n, on by default for new users. Turn off **Share usage data** in **Settings → Privacy & data** to stop new sends. [Your data and privacy](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/trust/privacy/) lists exactly what is sent.
Does it work when my laptop is closed?
Not yet. [Schedules](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/use/schedules/) run while the computer that runs Nod is on. Run it on a [Mac mini](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/deploy/mac-mini/) or [your own server](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/deploy/self-host/) to keep it always on. A hosted version is next on the list.
Can it make mistakes?
Yes. Its [safety check](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/trust/) is a model's judgement, and Nod is a research preview. That is why it asks before anything you didn't ask for, and why everything it did is on record. Pick a capable model. In 240 test decisions, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 got every one right. Claude Haiku 5.5 let 8 unsafe actions through.

Install the app, connect a model and your apps, then ask for something
in the app, on Telegram, or on WhatsApp. Setup takes about ten minutes.

Run from source
On macOS or Linux, install Node.js 24.21 or later, pnpm, and Docker. Then run: ```sh git clone https://github.com/n8n-io/nod.git cd nod corepack enable pnpm start ``` See [Install from source](https://nod.n8n.io/docs/get-started/install-from-source/) for the Linux Vault key and access link, and [`docs/`](docs/README.md) for the docs of this revision.

Nod is open source, from the team behind n8n.
Read CONTRIBUTING to send your first change.

Creating your own connectors
Use MCP, an HTTP API, or a CLI. Add an app folder, run the required tests, and submit a PR.
The guide includes an AI builder skill, approval requirements, and shareable app pages.
